subject.title: [Feature]: Support custom HTTP headers on CLI WebSocket connections

question: Should OpenClaw add custom Gateway CLI WebSocket headers, and which credential-safe sources and precedence should be supported?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but the requested flag/env/config surfaces can carry reverse-proxy credentials and change the Gateway authentication boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Approve a narrow secret-safe contract
options.body: Add header forwarding only through maintainer-approved sources, with SecretInput/env substitution, redaction, docs, and tests for fresh and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Limit to explicit CLI headers only
options.body: Avoid durable config/env persistence for now and require operators to pass headers explicitly per invocation, reducing secret-storage surface at the cost of automation ergonomics.

options.title: Decline core header support
options.body: Keep SSH, Tailscale, and local proxy workflows as the supported paths and document that authenticating reverse-proxy header injection stays outside OpenClaw CLI.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow secret-safe contract
recommendation.body: Add header forwarding only through maintainer-approved sources, with SecretInput/env substitution, redaction, docs, and tests for fresh and upgrade behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is ownership of the gateway-client package extraction and Gateway call boundary that would need the new contract.
